methodological_rigor.justification: This is a single-center retrospective cohort of 575 advanced (AJCC 8th edition stage IIIB/IV) lung adenocarcinoma patients from 2010-2019, analyzing overall survival versus clinical, metastatic-site, biomarker (EGFR/ALK/PD-L1/CEA), and treatment variables. The observational design can support prognostic associations but is vulnerable to confounding by indication and selection biases; the methods explicitly note that no other specific inclusion/exclusion criteria were applied beyond diagnosis and data availability. Statistically, the paper uses time-to-event methods (Kaplan-Meier/log-rank), multivariable Cox regression, and multiple survival-ML models with repeated 70/30 splits and C-index/time-dependent AUC evaluation, but it excludes patients with missing data from Cox analyses and does not describe strategies for confounding control beyond regression.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work is an individual cohort study of real-world advanced lung adenocarcinoma patients assessing OS, so it maps to Oxford LoE 2b. Clinical relevance is direct because the endpoints are patient-relevant (OS) and the predictors include actionable biomarkers and treatment strategies (e.g., EGFR mutation status/subtypes, TKI choice, bevacizumab exposure). The translational value is mainly prognostic/risk-stratification rather than causal comparative effectiveness, given the retrospective non-randomized design.

reporting_quality.justification: As a retrospective observational cohort, STROBE is the appropriate reporting standard. The manuscript describes setting and time window, cohort size, key variable definitions (e.g., smoking categories, biomarker ascertainment, 70/30 train-test splits for ML), and core survival/statistical methods including handling of suspected non-proportional hazards via a two-stage hazard rate comparison approach. However, reporting is weakened by limited explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria beyond data availability, exclusion of missing data without imputation, and incomplete detail on model tuning/calibration and external validation. No data or code deposition is described for the clinical dataset or the ML pipelines.

novelty_literature.justification: The clinical findings (EGFR mutation associated with longer OS; comparisons across common EGFR subtypes; TKI and bevacizumab associations) are generally consistent with established precision-oncology themes, making much of the contribution incremental. The more distinctive element is packaging a decade-long single-center dataset with multiple survival-focused ML models and reporting C-index and time-dependent AUC comparisons. Overall novelty is moderate, leaning toward method/application rather than a fundamentally new biological or clinical insight.

writing_presentation.justification: The abstract and results provide concrete cohort counts and effect summaries (e.g., OS medians for EGFR-mutant vs wild-type; afatinib vs first-generation TKIs; bevacizumab exposure groups). Methods are structured with separate subsections for each modeling approach and describe evaluation metrics (C-index and time-dependent AUC) and survival-testing choices including non-proportional-hazards considerations. Some implementation details are abbreviated (e.g., partial truncation of package citation in the normalized text and limited description of feature processing), but overall organization is clear.

key_strengths: Large real-world cohort (n=575) of advanced lung adenocarcinoma with OS endpoint and clinically actionable biomarker/treatment variables (EGFR/ALK/PD-L1; TKI choice; bevacizumab exposure).

Uses multiple survival analysis approaches (Kaplan-Meier/log-rank, multivariable Cox, and several survival-ML models) with discrimination metrics (C-index and time-dependent AUC) and acknowledges non-proportional hazards via a two-stage approach.
key_concerns: Retrospective single-center design with high risk of confounding by indication for treatment comparisons (e.g., TKI choice and bevacizumab exposure) and limited description of how confounding was addressed beyond regression.
Missing data are handled by exclusion in multivariable Cox analyses without sensitivity analysis or imputation, risking bias and reduced generalizability.
No external validation and no shared data/code for the ML pipelines, limiting reproducibility and confidence in the prognostic model claims.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is clinically relevant, competently analyzed retrospective prognostic work with moderate novelty, but it needs stronger STROBE-style transparency, missing-data handling, confounding discussion, and validation before being competitive beyond a mid-tier observational oncology venue.
